summary: A tab takes dropped items, closes on a middle click, has Close Other Tabs in its menu, and shows its name while it is dragged. src/finder/tab_bar.rs, `render_tab_bar`: every tab but the one showing carries the folder its browser shows (`drop_folder()`, so none for search results, Recents, results sent from Nushell or the Trash) and is wrapped in `transfer::folder_drop_target`; the browser that draws the bar runs the transfer. A middle press on a tab defers `Workspace::close_tab_at_press(id, click_count, ..)`. The tab's menu has Close Other Tabs between Close Tab and Move Tab to New Window. A dragged tab draws `list::DragLabel` with its title; `DraggedTab`'s empty `Render` impl is gone. src/workspace.rs: `close_other_tabs`, `close_tab_at_press`, and a field `closed_by_press` (whether the last change to the tabs was a tab closed by a middle press on it), which `tabs_changed` clears. src/finder/views.rs: the two middle-press handlers of the views (`item_interactions` for list, icons and gallery, and the column view's row) go through `middle_press_on_folder`, which opens nothing for a press that `Presses::is_stray` takes for the rest of a double press. src/finder/list.rs: `DragLabel` has the ID `drag-label`, an aria label and `test_support()`. docs/manual.md: the Tabs paragraph and two bullets under Dragging and dropping. tests/common/mod.rs: `nth_click_point_with` and `drop_from_another_app`.
changelog: Tabs take more from the mouse. Drop items on another tab to move them into the folder it shows, or to copy them, by the same rules as a drop on a folder; files from other apps are copied in. Middle-click a tab to close it. A tab's right-click menu has Close Other Tabs, which leaves only that tab. And a tab being dragged shows its name under the mouse. A double middle-click on a folder now opens that folder alone, where its second click also opened the folder under the pointer in the new tab.
behaviour_changes: Items dragged onto a tab other than the one showing go into the folder that tab shows: they move, or are copied with the copy key (Option on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) or when any is on another volume. A name clash asks as for any drop, and Replace and Undo work as they do there (probed in review: Replace, Undo, Undo again puts back what was replaced). The tab is drawn in the drop-target colour while such a drag is over it. The tab the items went to reloads, the window stays on the tab it showed, and split view's pane reloads too when the items came from it (probed by both). Tested for move, copy, the reload and no change of tab; pictured in light and dark by both.
Files dragged in from another app and dropped on such a tab are copied into its folder. Tested (added in review). Not run on a real desktop.

The tab that shows takes nothing, and has no highlight: the folder it stands for is the one in the window. Tested in review with files from another app, where a mistake would show (items of the window's own folder dropped there would stay put either way); pictured. A tab showing search results takes nothing (tested), nor one showing Recents or the Trash (probed in review), nor results sent from Nushell (by reading: `drop_folder()` has none). Nor do the + and the empty part of the bar (probed in review).

A folder dropped on the tab that shows that same folder does nothing, with no message, and the next drag works (probed by both). Dropped on a tab showing a folder inside it, the existing warning about a folder going into itself shows and nothing moves. Items dropped on a tab that shows the folder they are already in stay put; with the copy key a copy is made there ("notes copy.txt"). The last two are the implementer's probes.
A drop on a tab whose folder has gone from disk moves nothing and says why in the usual error notice (probed in review).

A press of the middle button on a tab, its close button included, closes that tab at once, on the press, as the other middle-button actions. The window stays on the tab that shows unless that was the one closed, in which case the files of the tab that takes over get the keyboard. Tested for a background tab and the showing tab. With a tab's menu open, a middle press on a tab beside the menu closes the menu and the tab, and the files have the keyboard (probed in review). In split view the first pane's files get the keyboard even when the other pane had it, as after a click on a tab's × (probed in review for both).

Quick presses of the middle button at one spot close one tab after another: each closes the tab that the one before it brought under the pointer, also when the tab closed was the one showing, so that another browser draws the bar for the next press. Tested (added in review). With three or more tabs a double press therefore closes two, as a double-click on a tab's × does.

From the review: the rest of a double press of the middle button does nothing else. When the press before it closed the second-last tab, and the tab bar went with it, it opens no folder that is under the pointer now (tested in the icon and column views; the list's header and the gallery had nothing there to open). On the implementer's commit it opened that folder in a new tab, which the implementer had reported.

From the review: a double press of the middle button on a folder opens the folder in one tab and closes none. With one tab, the new tab brings the tab bar, and a folder in the top 32 points of the files (the first row of the column view and the top of its second, the upper part of the first row of icons, the top few points of the list's first row) is then under a tab, the first tab for the folders at the left. On the implementer's commit the second press closed that tab, the one the folder was pressed in, with its history: the window was left with the new tab alone (probed in the column view). Tested.

From the review, and changing what the trunk did before this improvement: a double press of the middle button on a folder in a view opens that folder only. Before, the second press opened the folder under the pointer in the new tab in a third tab, and in split view's other pane, which doesn't change, it opened a second tab at the same folder (the pane is the review's probe: one tab now). Every further press in the same row is left alone too, until the system starts counting again (a pause, or the mouse moved). Tested for the first case.

A tab's right-click menu has a third item, Close Other Tabs, between Close Tab and Move Tab to New Window. It closes every tab but the one right-clicked, shows that one, and gives its files the keyboard; the tab bar goes, since one tab has none. Split view's other pane stays, and loses the keyboard to the kept tab, as with Close Tab. Tested for a background tab and for the showing tab; pictured in light and dark. A double-click on the item does nothing to the files that come under the pointer when the bar goes (probed in review in the icon view: nothing opened or selected).

A tab being dragged shows its full title in a label under the mouse, in the look a dragged favorite has; before, nothing was drawn. The label sits where the tab's corner was relative to the pointer, so with a wide tab grabbed in its middle it is some way left of the pointer. Tested, pictured in light and dark.
The drag label of favorites and column headers has an accessibility label (its text) and the element ID drag-label; it looks the same.

docs/manual.md says the above in the Tabs paragraph (middle-click, drop on another tab and which tabs take none, that holding items over a tab doesn't show it, the three menu items) and names another tab in two bullets under Dragging and dropping. The rules for quick presses are not in the manual.
left_out: Holding a drag over a tab doesn't show the tab (plan of record: no `spring_loaded`, which would take the showing browser to the tab's folder). Finder shows the tab after a moment. Probed by the implementer: held 3 seconds, nothing changes, and letting go then moves the item.
The tab that shows is not a drop target (plan of record).
Close Other Tabs is only in a tab's menu: no menu-bar item, action or key (not in the brief).
A tab closed by mistake can't be brought back: there is no Reopen Closed Tab, and neither a middle click nor Close Other Tabs asks first. Close Tab is the same.

A transfer still running in a tab that a middle click or Close Other Tabs closes finishes on disk (what it replaced still goes to the Trash, from the transfer's own thread) but records no Undo and tells no other tab, as after Close Tab. The verifier's accepted risk; read in `run_transfer`, not probed.
Sidebar rows and path bar crumbs keep their middle-press handlers as they were: a double press there opens two tabs (see Found, not fixed).
The dragged tab's label is placed like every drag label in the app, by the corner of what was grabbed. The verifier called it cosmetic.

review_fixes: A bug in what the change added, which nobody had seen: with one tab, a double press of the middle button on a folder near the top of the files closed the tab the folder was pressed in. The first press opens the folder in a second tab, which brings the tab bar, and the bar comes where the top 36 points of the files were; the second press lands on the first tab, which is the original one, and the new middle-click close closed it. Reproduced on 4a66e39 in the column view (a press 6 points into the first folder's row: two tabs after the first press, one after the second, the original gone with its history and place). The first row of the column view, the top of its second, and the upper part of the first row of icons are in reach, so a worn middle button that fires twice is enough. Fix: `Workspace::close_tab_at_press`, which the tab's handler now calls with the press's click count. A press counted second or later closes a tab only when the last change to the tabs was a tab closed by such a press (`closed_by_press`, cleared in `tabs_changed`, so opening, selecting, moving or otherwise closing a tab ends a row). Quick closes in a row still work, across a change of the browser that draws the bar, which is why the record is the window's and not a browser's. Test a_double_middle_click_on_a_folder_opens_one_tab_and_closes_none.

The side effect the implementer reported and left out as a separate change: with two tabs, a second quick middle press where the closed tab was opened the folder that had come under the pointer in a new tab (probed again: icon view at both tabs' spots, column view at the first's; a third press then closed a tab again, since the bar was back). It is this change's doing, and the same remedy closes the fault that was there before (a double press on a folder opening two tabs), so I made it here: `Finder::middle_press_on_folder` in src/finder/views.rs, called by both of the views' middle-press handlers, opens nothing when `Presses::is_stray(click_count)`, the rule the left button has for the rest of a double-click on something outside the views. A middle press is not written into that record, so every further press in the row is left alone, which suits a button with no double-click of its own. Test quick_middle_clicks_at_one_spot_close_tabs_and_open_no_folder, and the second half of the other new test.

A test for files dropped from another app, which the implementer had no way to send: gpui's `FileDropEvent` can be dispatched like any input, and `Ui::drop_from_another_app` does that. dropping_on_a_tab_moves_or_copies_into_its_folder now drops a file from another folder on the tab (copied in, the original stays, the tab reloads) and on the tab that shows (nothing), which is also the first test that pins that the showing tab takes no items.

Commit message: the paragraph that said a second quick press was left unchanged is replaced by what happens now and why, and the Changelog paragraph has a sentence for the double middle-click on a folder.

notes:

The next integration has carried it since: by the time this record was written the trunk had moved on by one commit (1acaff3, thumbnail-memory), which is after this one, and origin/search-ui-polish was at 1acaff3 too. How it was checked. With the implementer's src diff reverse-applied on their commit, their five tests fail for the brief's reasons (Projects/notes.txt missing; (3, 2) where (2, 1); no menu item Close Other Tabs; the two-item menu; no element drag-label), and tabs_and_split_view passes. With the trunk commit's src diff reverse-applied, all seven fail (the two added in review too) and tabs_and_split_view passes; the tree was clean after applying it again, both times. Seven mutations of the final code, one at a time, each caught: no `is_stray` check in `middle_press_on_folder`; the column row calling `open_in_new_tabs` directly; `close_tab_at_press` always closing; never closing for a press counted second or later; no reset in `tabs_changed`; the flag never set; the showing tab given a drop folder. The implementer's mutations I did not run again; two of theirs survive, as they said: `close_other_tabs` without `leave_active_tab` (the right press that opens the menu has already ended any name that can be kept, so nothing can show it) and without `tabs_changed` (the focus change redraws). Both lines stay: the first is what every change of the showing tab does, and the second now also ends a row of middle presses. The seven tests pass with SEED=0, 1, 7, 42, 99, 1234 and 31337 and in 15 iterations, on the trunk commit. Probes were a throwaway tests/zz_probe_review.rs, removed before the check, kept as text beside the pictures. I took twelve pictures of my own (six states, light and dark) from the code with the review's fixes, looked at each, and compared them with the implementer's: the same in every state.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the probes say. (1) A tab is closed that nobody meant to close, and it cannot be brought back. That was real: see review_fixes, the first. What is left is by convention: a double press on a tab with three or more tabs closes two, as a double-click on a × does, and Close Other Tabs is next to Close Tab in the menu. A stale menu cannot close the wrong tab: its items carry the browser's ID, not the tab's place, and a tab that has gone is not found (`close_tab` and `close_other_tabs` both return). (2) Items go somewhere the person did not mean or cannot see. The folder a tab takes items into is read from the tab's browser in the same frame as the title on the tab, so the two cannot disagree, and a drag redraws the window with every move of the mouse, so the folder is as of the last move. A hidden tab's place only changes by its own navigation, which needs it showing. The showing tab, and tabs of searches, Recents and the Trash, take nothing. The move is the showing browser's: its progress row, its name-clash question, and Undo from any tab. The drop handlers are of three different types on one element; gpui takes the drag once per matching listener and would panic on two of one type, and there is one of each. (3) The window is left in a state that takes no keys or draws a menu for a tab that has gone. After every close the files of the tab that shows have the keyboard (tested for the middle click and both forms of Close Other Tabs; probed with a menu open, with the search field holding the keyboard by the implementer, and in split view). A closed tab's browser is released (tested), and its Quick Look window closes with it (`observe_release_in`, by reading). A tab's menu is drawn from element state under the tab's place, and the next menu on a tab at that place is that tab's own (probed).

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. On a Mac check once: files dragged from Finder onto another tab are copied in and Option-drag from fffinder copies; a mouse's middle button closes a tab; a double press of it on a folder in the first rows of the column view, with one tab, opens one tab and closes none. The click counts are the system's (NSEvent's on macOS, per button on Linux and Windows by the kit's own count). If macOS counts a left click and a middle click at one spot as one row, a middle click on a tab straight after a click on another tab's × at that spot does nothing once, and the next one works. (b) A middle click closes without asking and there is no way to reopen a tab. With three or more tabs a button that fires twice closes two. If that is too easy to do by accident, `close_tab_at_press` is the one place: refuse every press counted second or later, at the price of quick closes in a row. (c) After a folder opened in a second tab right under the pointer, a deliberate middle click on that tab at the same spot does nothing until the system's double-click time has passed. (d) Holding a drag over a tab does not show the tab, where Finder does. (e) Close Other Tabs has no key and is not in the menu bar. (f) The label of a dragged tab can sit up to a tab's width left of the pointer.

For briefs still to come.
- split-active-pane: a middle click on a tab, Close Other Tabs and `close_tab` all end in `focus_active`, so the first pane takes the keyboard from the other pane (probed for the middle click and the ×). A drop on a tab is handled by the first pane's browser whichever pane the drag began in, and reloads both. `Workspace` has a new field `closed_by_press` and two new functions; whatever you add that changes the tabs or which one shows should end in `tabs_changed`, which clears the field. A tab's middle-press handler passes `event.click_count`; if panes get tab bars of their own, the record belongs to whatever owns that bar's tabs.
- restore-session-tabs: `Workspace` has a field `closed_by_press: bool`; a constructor shared with `new` sets it to false. `close_other_tabs` drops the other browsers, and close_other_tabs_keeps_the_one_clicked asserts one is released; if closed tabs are ever kept to be reopened, that assertion and closing_a_tab_stops_its_contents_search need the same answer. A tab's drop folder is `drop_folder()` of its browser as of each frame, so restored tabs need nothing.
- icon-tile-hit-target: `item_interactions`' middle handler now calls `middle_press_on_folder(folder, event.click_count, ..)`; keep that call. quick_middle_clicks_at_one_spot_close_tabs_and_open_no_folder presses, in the icon view, the spot where the first tab's middle was (18 points under the top of the files once the bar has gone, which is 9 points into the first tile, about where its icon begins) and expects a press of its own there to open the folder: it finds the tile by its bounds (`item_at`). If a tile's blank margin stops being the item, move that spot onto the icon, or the last assertion of the icon half fails. a_double_middle_click_on_a_folder_opens_one_tab_and_closes_none presses the centers of two tiles.
- column-row-menu-wrong-item: in `render_column_row` the middle handler, right under the right-press handler you change, is now `this.middle_press_on_folder(folder.clone(), event.click_count, window, cx)`. Nothing else there changed.
- fix-rename-press-selection, and anyone changing `Presses`: the views' middle handlers read `presses.is_stray(click_count)` and write nothing into the record. If a middle press on an item is ever recorded there, a double middle press on a folder in split view's other pane would count as two presses on the item and open two tabs again; the second half of a_double_middle_click_on_a_folder_opens_one_tab_and_closes_none would still pass, so probe it.
- name-clash-details, files-changed-off-thread: a drop on a tab goes through `drop_files`, `start_transfer` and `confirm_clashes` of the showing browser like any drop, and the tab it went to reloads through `files_changed` and `tell_others`. dropping_on_a_tab_moves_or_copies_into_its_folder reads the other tab's rows right after the drop has settled.
- context-menus-fit: a tab's menu has three short items now. Close Other Tabs always applies, since a tab bar needs two tabs. A file chooser has no tab bar.
- split-view-toolbar-clip: the two new tests in tests/basics.rs use a single pane at the default size and rely on the first tab being over the first tile and the first column (`item_at` and `tab.contains(&spot)` say so when it stops being true). None uses split view.
- collapsible-sidebar-sections, tree-arrows-past-smart-folder, and anyone testing a drag: a dragged favorite, column header or tab can be read in a test as the element `drag-label` (`ui.snapshot("drag-label").label()`), and files from another app can be dropped with `ui.drop_from_another_app(paths, id)`.
- fix-wording-after-later-changes: the manual's Tabs paragraph now lists what a tab takes from the mouse, and Dragging and dropping names another tab twice. CHANGELOG.md's own Tabs entry is as it was and still true; the new entry is this record's.
- stale-rows-on-place-change, inactive-selection-colour, view-switch-keeps-selection, content-match-highlight, multi-word-highlights, select-all-perf, thumbnail-memory, recent-searches, idle-redraw-after-search, go-to-folder-keyboard, path-bar-no-io: independent. The tab bar asks for no frame of its own for any of this, and reads one path per tab in each frame.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change, outside this brief).
- A double press of the middle button on a sidebar row (a place or a folder of the tree) or on a path bar crumb opens two tabs at that place: the row stays under the pointer, and its handler doesn't look at the click count (by reading sidebar.rs and bars.rs; the views had the same and are fixed here). Acting only on `event.click_count == 1` there would do.
- With one tab, Cmd+double-click on a folder near the top of the files opens it in a second tab, and a third click then lands on the tab bar that came and shows the first tab again (by reading: a tab's `on_click` takes any click).
- The doc comment of `copy_modifier` in src/finder/transfer.rs ("The key that makes a drag copy instead of move...") sits above `SetAside`'s doc comment, 35 lines from its function. `folder_drop_target`'s comment says a folder that can't take itself lets the drop go to the view around it; the kit takes the drag before it asks `can_drop`, so such a drop does nothing (the implementer's findings; the second probed on a tab by both).
- A transfer still running in a tab that closes, by any way of closing it, records no Undo and reloads no other tab when it ends. A tab could refuse to close, or hand its transfers to the window, while `transfers_running()`.
- A click on a background tab's × with the keyboard in split view's other pane gives the first pane the keyboard (probed). For split-active-pane.
- A middle press on an open menu does nothing and leaves the menu open (the kit's menus; seen in a probe).
